I guess most web sites pay for their operating costs by running ads. When you block an ad, at least in theory the website that you visit is "losing" revenue. What do you think?
Users of ad-blockers - How should websites pay for themselves?

They could have created a whole new business model for the new media, but they didn't. The reason companies are fucked is because they refuse to look for a different business model.

I startede using add blocking when websites began to run intrusive adds, eg. Add with moving/flashing and sound. And nowaday also because a lot of ad networks contains malware. This. Have no problem even with using more space. But same server and checked by the site owner. To be honest these ad networks are also the reason blockers work this well. Copy the ads to your server and ad blockers generally can't tell the difference. These are really ad network blockers, not ad blockers. I have no problem with seeing ads. But l I don't want the ad networks to track every page visit I make. This is nothing like ads in tv and newspapers. I visit an online shop, and the article I looked at greets me on every webpage for the next 5 days. Extra stupid when I bought it.

Website owners: Make ads and I will not block them. But I will block this tracking shit.
Find out how much 1 user actually costs, then you can ask people if they are willing to pay that.
And find a way to automate that payment, I dare say.
Life finds a way. Who knows what comes next after marketing user data, sponsored content, and paid shilling?

Let me buy my own ads. Websites only make fractions of pennies from each ad, and this is through an ad server company. I want to pay that ad server company $5 a month to not put ads on the pages I view. Websites still get paid.

I did not mind the small obscure yet noticeable ads that were on the side of a web page, and did not over take the purpose of the site I was visiting. When they turned into pop ups that appeared in the middle of your screen, tracked your private surfing habits, and you could not close the flash commercials thats when I started using them. I also use a stop script, and a ad block that works great.
Keep the ads, but allow viewers to pay $50 to electrically shock the ad designer's gonads if an individual viewer is especially annoyed by the ad design or content.

Websites should pay for themselves with news-paper style ads. This can get terribly out of hand because text can be embedded but it would make things look nice if on the side of the page there was a tiny paragraph about a product and no picture. That product cannot have gotten there because of your browsing activity and it can be relevant to the content. It's wrong to advertise your product within free services.
I really don't mind some side bar ads. I started using Adblock when all these websites started doing pop ups and pop unders and browser redirect. Just to frustrating to deal with.

IDGAF how websites pay for themselves. Figure it out.

But if their means of paying for themselves is obnoxious, then fuck them, I'm gonna use adblock.

If they annoy me, I'll annoy them right back.

I've had one of my domains and paid hosting since 2000, I pay half as much for Multiple times more storage and throughput. I guess I don't see where ads have improved the web, so I block them.

ads should be a fine way to pay for websites. but they need to get the message that intrusive ads should be done away with. but it's not getting through to them. Anyone using an ad blocker is probably smart enough to not click ads anyway. The masses will still click away.
